#2150. Barry Bannan reacts in two words to Jamal Lowe exploits for Sheffield Wednesday v Barnsley

Barry Bannan has issued a two-word reaction to the performance of Sheffield Wednesday teammate, Jamal Lowe, as the Owls made it two league victories in succession under newly-appointed head coach, Dave Challinor.

Having seen off Plymouth Argyle last Saturday, Challinor's first League One outing in charge of Wednesday on the road came in the form of a South Yorkshire derby against Daniel Stendel's lowly Barnsley outfit.

Backed by over 4,800 supporters, Challinor's side didn't disappoint as they raced into a two-goal lead within the first 14 minutes, with Lowe netting his first brace of the campaign.

The Tykes responded five minutes before half-time through the highly-rated Vimal Yonganathan, but back-to-back victories for the first time since September lifted the Owls up to third.

Upon taking the managerial role at Hillsborough, Challinor has plenty of quality and experience at his disposal, with both attributes possessed by Bannan and Lowe in particular.

The latter opened the scoring at Oakwell just eight minutes into the encounter as he side-footed Liam Cooper's knockdown from a free-kick past Cieran Slicker, before doubling the advantage six minutes later as he was found in acres of space by Bannan, then drifting inside and slotting the ball into the bottom-right-hand corner.

Those strikes were the Jamaican's first since his dramatic 98th-minute penalty against Huddersfield Town last month, taking his overall tally up to seven for the season.

Speaking post-match, Lowe claimed that he is capable of taking his tally up to 15 goals, which will be music to the ears of Owls fans, as well as Bannan, who issued a two-word reaction of: "Goals Like", with a picture of him and the versatile figure in celebration.

Across his 93 appearances for the Owls, Lowe has endured a mixed time, even after producing seven goal contributions last term.

In the wins over Plymouth and Barnsley, the 32-year-old has been stationed at left-wing-back, and received praise for his all-round performance from many Wednesdayites.

"Testament to the new manager people say oh J Lowe is lazy can’t run etc and not only does Dave have him run he puts him at LWB where he has to run and gets goals from there on top," said one of those supporters.

Another Wednesday fan commented: "Gave Jamal Lowe stick last couple of weeks but effort for tonight was brilliant. Credit where credits due well done 2 goals along the way! Long may it continue. Honolulu Wednesday!!!"

"Jamal Lowe has turned into peak Roberto Carlos," was a rather humourous summation of his exploits.

Owls fans, how did you view Jamal Lowe's all-round performance against Barnsley? Comment below!

Another verdict read: "Playing Lowe in (his) best position. GOAL. Well done Jamz."

However, not all were overly convinced, with one supporter claiming: "Lowe has no clue how to defend."

Challinor recently went viral due to an image of his notes during the FA Cup defeat to Oldham Athletic in his first game in charge, and despite a youthful side being defeated heavily in the EFL Trophy to Accrington Stanley, his league ventures have started strongly.

Wednesday are still not flawless, but the outlook of their season is certainly more rosey than in the final weeks of Henrik Pedersen's tenure, as they can only drop to fifth depending on Saturday's results.

FLW have ranked the 10 best EFL League One stadiums so far in the 2026/27 season, including Bradford City and Sheffield Wednesday.

With Plymouth expected to challenge for promotion, last weekend's 3-0 success was seen as a statement, whilst different characteristics earned three points against their local rivals.

Challinor will now hope his side benefit from an extra day's recovery for when they travel to Stevenage on Tuesday.

Manchester United are prepared to consider legal action if evidence emerges that another club approached academy forward JJ Gabriel without permission.

The 16-year-old announced his departure from Old Trafford in a social media video on Tuesday and is expected to join Real Madrid in January. According to The Times and ESPN, United remain concerned about the circumstances surrounding his proposed move, although no breach of transfer regulations has been established.

Gabriel has been absent from United since September, when he requested the cancellation of his registration. The teenager remains registered with the club, and United could explore legal or regulatory options if evidence of an unauthorised approach emerges.

The Independent reports that United do not want to punish Gabriel for actions they believe may have been taken by adults involved in his future. Real Madrid have been widely linked with the forward, but his transfer has not been formally completed.

Gabriel joined United’s academy in 2020 and was named the club’s young player of the year last season. He featured for the senior side during pre-season but has not made a competitive first-team appearance.

The youngster is eligible for a move within the European Union under an exception to FIFA’s rules on international transfers involving players aged under 18. In his farewell message, Gabriel thanked United for helping him develop during his six years at the club.

His expected move to Madrid would bring that association to an end, although questions remain over the process leading to his departure. United have not announced legal proceedings, and there has been no finding of wrongdoing by Real Madrid or any other club.

#2147. What Dave Challinor said after Sheffield Wednesday win has sparked a reaction

The new Sheffield Wednesday manager had qualified praise for his team's performance following his team's South Yorkshire derby win at Barnsley.

Following a slightly rocky start, Dave Challinor is starting to settle in as the new manager of Sheffield Wednesday. Two Jamal Lowe goals in the opening stages of their Friday night trip to Barnsley gave them the perfect start at Oakwell, but Wednesday were pegged back by a goal from Vimal Yoganathan and ended up hanging on a little for the win.

The three points lifted them to third place in the table, though as this was a Friday night fixture, they might well not still be there by the end of the weekend, and after the match Challinor had some praise for his team's performance, though he was very clear that they still have a lot of work to do to get the team to the level of the manager's satisfaction.

Speaking to the Sheffield Wednesday media team after his team's win at Barnsley as posted to the social media platfiorm X, Challinor was qualified in praise of his team's performance: "I'm really pleased with the win. I won't say I'm disappointed with our performance, but I think there's loads more to come from us. As I've just said to the players, my job's not to really over-celebrate wins, it's to look at things analytically and make sure we're better, and there's stacks more to come from us."

And it's clear that Challinor wants to see his team playing on the front foot more: "Scoring two goals is the best thing that could happen and probably the worst thing too because, from a player's perspective, we became really passive, too negative, and almost thought the game was won. We have and will continue to take ourselves out of our comfort zone and expose ourselves a little bit. We need to defend miles higher up."

What tweaks would you want made to the Sheffield Wednesday team during the January transfer window? Let us know in the comments below!

Asked about the performance of Jamal Lowe, Challinor revealed that the forward was disappointed not to receive the Man of the Match Award, given his two goals: "It's nice to score from a set-piece again. Jamal's done another brilliant job for the team in a position that's not his position, but he's got two goals from there, which is great for him, and on another day he gets himself a hat-trick, potentially. Strangely, he hasn't got the Match of the Match from Sky, which he's disappointed about, but we can deal with that because we've got three points."

And he also singled out Liam Cooper for praise: "Coops is a leader for us. With him, his experience and his age, he is going to be important, but as I've told him, I've got to get him to get the rest of them up the pitch and not be defending too deep. I've been there. The last thing you want to be is a centre-half who's not rapid against strikers who want to run in behind, looking behind and having loads of space between your backside and your own goal. But it's going to paramount to what we do and how we go about it. And for him to get through two 90 minutes in the last week is brilliant for us. We've got to recover and make sure we're good to go on Tuesday."

Sheffield Wednesday's 2-1 win at Barnsley continued their uplift under Dave Challinor. Defeat away to League Two Oldham Athletic in the FA Cup was not the result that anyone at Hillsborough was expecting from his first match in charge, but his team has recovered well in the two games since then, with a convincing 3-0 win against Plymouth Argyle in his first home match as manager followed by a welcome derby win away from home at Barnsley.

The win pushed Wednesday up to third place in the League One table, though it's unlikely they'll still be there by the end of the weekend. Fourth-placed Oxford United are at home to Wycombe Wanderers, while fifth-placed Luton Town are away to Burton Albion. #2145. Who stays and who leaves Manchester United under Mauricio Pochettino, Gary Neville reveals list

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United hired Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, who managed just one win in 10 games.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United sitting in an unfamiliar 18th in the Premier League table with only one win from 10 matches. He has a massive job ahead of him, with many pundits and former players terming his situation the toughest in the Premier League.

Gary Neville believes the Argentine will need several transfer windows to get the squad where he wants it, if he gets that much of time at Manchester United.

The former captain shared his views on which players he expects Pochettino to keep, and who could be heading for the exit.

Neville believes Senne Lammens should remain part of the plans, although he expects Pochettino to bring in another goalkeeper to give him some competition for his place. At the back, he backed Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire and Leny Yoro to stay, while suggesting Ayden Heaven needs a loan move to the Championship.

“Heaven, I’d loan him out, get some experience in the Championship. He’s nowhere near it, it’s unfair to put him in the situation he’s in,” Neville said on Stick to Football.

In midfield, Neville wants Pochettino to build around Bruno Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans. He also believes Andrey Santos could have a future at the club because of his age, mobility and aggression.

Mason Mount, however, is not part of his plans. Neville said: “Mount would have to go” and identified him as the player to leave from that midfield group.

Neville also has his doubts on the forward line, with much of the front line seeing a change. Gary Neville expects Joshua Zirkzee to leave and believes United cannot continue paying Marcus Rashford’s wages.

“Zirkzee definitely to go. I think Marcus 100 per cent to go because he’s on massive money and that story has been well told. They can’t afford to pay him that money, you have to get rid of that wage at the earliest opportunity.”

He expects Pochettino to work with Amad Diallo, Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Sesko. Patrick Dorgu could also be useful in the short term, although Neville thinks he may leave within the next couple of years. Manuel Ugarte, meanwhile, was another player he was certain would go.

Talking about the exits, Gary Neville has singled out many United stars to be shown the door in the first wave of squad clearance by Mauricio Pochettino. Neville identified Lisandro Martínez, Matthijs de Ligt and Noussair Mazraoui as further candidates to leave in the first wave of departures, alongside Mount, Rashford and Zirkzee.

Neville believes another group of exits could follow a year later, with Shaw, Maguire, Diogo Dalot and Fernandes among the players whose futures may not be at the club in long term. Pochettino would also have to decide whether Santos and Carlos Baleba fit into his long-term plans.

Neville does not expect United to rebuild the squad in a single summer, even if Pochettino makes a positive start.

“But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.”

Pochettino’s first game comes against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday. His immediate priority will be to get some results for Manchester United but beyond the immediate games and results, Manchester United are expected to make multiple exits from the club as Pochettino settles into the job.

#2144. Ex-pro boxer names England's 5 hardest football firms

One of the major shifts to domestic football in the last thirty years comes in the form of football hooliganism, which has received particular police attention and continues to be clamped down by the authorities.

The hooliganism subculture enjoyed its peak between the 1970s and 1990s, as fans throughout the width and breadth of the country organised themselves into factions and travelled in numbers to fight it out with opposition supporters.

It still happens today, of course, but on a far-less-frequent and much more heavily policed scale, with the authorities having taken considerable action against those involved in organised matchday violence over the years.

That doesn't stop punters from debating who the best firms are, though, as not only do some exist to this day, but they also hold a certain level of nostalgia to some.

During hooliganism's heyday, the likes of Birmingham City, Cardiff, Chelsea, Middlesbrough, Millwall, Portsmouth and West Ham were all regarded among the toughest and most violent fanbases in the country. Much has changed since those dark days, however, and where do those firms rank now?

Anthony Phythian, a former professional boxer from Manchester who followed Man City home and away and threw hands both in the ring and on the terraces, was asked to name the FIVE hardest firms he encountered when speaking on Daniel Wright's 'Northern Monkeys' podcast.

Phythian evaded a case of club-rivalry bias by initiating proceedings with a mention of bitter cross-city foes Manchester United, who have always had a bit of a reputation off the pitch as well as on it.

Quite naturally, of course, the ex-boxer will have crossed paths and exchanged blows with those on the red side of Manchester on countless occasions, and despite the fierceness of the rivalry that only ever limits praise across the city's divide, he does believe that the Old Trafford faithful were once among the hardest firms in the land.

Speaking on United, Phythian explained: "Gotta have United, because they've been our biggest rivals over the years.

A Home Office study has revealed which fanbases have seen the most arrests in English football, with those of some EFL clubs ranking high

"To be fair, they are a good lot, they've got a good firm, they're a game lot and they've got numbers."

That's one element that always came to the Red Devils' aid when engaging in matchday warfare, where they could often outnumber opposing firms due to the sheer size of the club and its fanbase.

United hooligans would gain notoriety during the 1974/75 season when the club were positioned inside the old Second Division, and groups such as the Red Army and Inter City Jibbers made quite the name for themselves back in the day.

As previously alluded to, Birmingham City once had one of English football's most notorious and identifiable firms.

Whereas the overwhelming majority of hooligan groups were predominantly white and often included affiliations to far-right factions, the so-called 'Zulu Warriors' earned their name after Man City's lot chanted "Zulu, Zulu" at Bluenoses in 1982.

The name stuck and Birmingham, whose firm obtained a rather unique reputation for having a mixed-ethnicity group courtesy of the city's diversity and multiculturalism, chose to adopt it as their own.

The 'Zulu Warriors' were particularly violent in their pomp and were subjected to numerous police raids and operations, such as the well-documented 'Operation Red Card' relating to disorder against local rivals Wolves, and few firms attracted greater fear from opposition supporters.

That's exactly why Phythian, in his own words, would "have them up there".

Stoke City, meanwhile, were never regarded among the very best firms, but those on pre-2000s terraces across the land who embroiled in organised matchday violence will always sing the Potters' praises in this genre.

Phythian believes that the Potters "definitely" need to be in the conversation and, akin to United and Birmingham, not too many fans will disagree with his claim.

Stoke's more recent reputation, albeit back in the Premier League days under Tony Pulis and the like, revolves around being on the pitch, but, some years previously, was all about being even more formidable away from it.

Their 'Norty Forty' firm certainly lived up to its name, and is believed to have included more than 700 members at its peak. Stoke always travelled in numbers and had no shortage of punters willing to scrap it out on a Saturday, with some particularly-unsavory incidents emerging.

In October 2001, 84 people were arrested following wholesale violence in the Potteries derby between Stoke and Port Vale as around 300 police officers were enlisted on the footballing frontlines that day. That same season would see a staggering 1,000 officers on duty for Stoke's home clash against the aforementioned Cardiff, which was halted for seven minutes owing to widespread fan arrests.

As for Everton, who have also been named as one of Phythian's five picks, the Toffees had the tendency for trouble without being classified as one of the country's leading firms.

The self-proclaimed 'County Road Cutters' had their name from both the long road that led up to Everton's former Goodison Park alongside their deplorable use of Stanley knives in matchday battles, which tells you just about everything you need to know.

Everton's perennial top-flight status means that they represent a group of supporters who Phythian would've had plenty of altercations with, and although they wouldn't necessarily be among everybody's five toughest firms, they're certainly up there as far as he's concerned.

They gained their biggest scalp against Manchester United fans back in 2005, which reportedly left around 100 'Red Army' members bloodied and injured in what is known as 'The Battle of Everton Valley'.

It's moments like those, however violent and unsavoury, that will be in Phythian's thinking.

Phythian rounded off by listing Tottenham Hotspur, which may represent something of a surprise as the only London-based inclusion in the ex-fighter's thinking.

He didn't want to include the Lilywhites, either, as he remarked: "I'd have Tottenham. To be fair, as much as it kills me, they're probably the best (firm) out of London in my time going.

"They've always had numbers, have been pretty organised and are the best lads out of London."

Hooligans in support of Chelsea, Millwall and West Ham would likely disagree with Phythian's claim, and there's no denying that the trio have a greater notoriety for matchday-related violence over the years than Spurs typically do.

What do you make of these claims? Which club do you think has the toughest firm in English football? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

But that's not to say that Spurs fans can't get up to all sorts of trouble either, and some would argue that their firm is often overlooked in hooliganism-centred discourse.

Spurs' exploits in Europe, which notably included riots against Feyenoord fans during the 1974 UEFA Cup final, gave the North Londoners a name on the continent, and that particular incident is widely-believed to have introduced hooliganism to the Netherlands.

They're often well up for it when it comes to local derbies against the likes of Arsenal and Chelsea, too, and they have been known to cause lots of trouble over the years.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

The Stoke lads earned respect across the country, and among those who lived through that era, Stoke City will always be in the conversation as one of the hardest firms in the Uk

#2142. How can Mauricio Pochettino help Manchester United players to perform again?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Mauricio Pochettino has called on Manchester United to rediscover their winning mentality after agreeing to become the club’s new head coach.

Manchester United announced Pochettino’s appointment just over 24 hours after confirming the departure of Michael Carrick. The former Chelsea and Tottenham manager is believed to have agreed a two-and-a-half-year deal at Old Trafford.

He takes charge of United who sit in an embarrassing 18th place in the Premier League table. They have managed just one win in their opening 10 league matches, coming against Ipswich Town.

There is little time for the new head coach to settle in, with a difficult first fixture against fierce rivals, Liverpool already awaiting him.

Speaking to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino made it clear that restoring confidence in the team and improving performances will be his immediate priorities.

“The most important thing for now is to start to work hard to recover that feeling about being a winner – to win games, to perform.”

The Argentine hinted at sticking with the current crop of players to help them rediscover their form.

“We need to love the players that we have. We need to support the players, we need to provide all the tools for them to perform.”

Pochettino’s first match in charge will be one of the toughest possible introductions to English football’s biggest rivalry. Manchester United travel to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday, giving Pochettino very little time to work with his squad before his first outing.

The new head coach faces a mountain ahead of him. He has walked into one of the most difficult jobs in world football. United have struggled so far into the season and they need results quickly to get them out of the relegation spots.

Pochettino has spoken about bringing back the winning feeling at Old Trafford, but his first challenge will be getting a response from his players who have managed only one league win in 10 games so far. That is far from Manchester United standards and Pochettino will be hoping he can instill some confidence back in the team.

The Liverpool game will offer an early indication of how his players respond to the change at United. A positive result would provide immediate relief for the under pressure United but the longer-term job of rebuilding United will take much more than one match.

#2140. What did the secret drone footage reveal about Manchester United training?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session was secretly filmed by a drone operator, who has since apologised and removed the footage from his YouTube channel after admitting his actions were unethical.

The footage showed players split into smaller groups carrying out different drills. On a separate full-size pitch, 11 players were positioned across the field alongside mannequins before gathering to receive instructions and feedback from new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Ten players were seen working with Pochettino in the video but only Harry Maguire, Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo are regular starters among those.

Another group involved in drills was that of Lisandro Martinez, Matthijs de Ligt, Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount, Leny Yoro, Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot.

In his statement, the operator said the flight itself was legal under drone regulations but accepted that recording the training session was wrong.

He explained that his intention was to give Manchester United supporters their first look at Pochettino wearing the club’s training kit.

He said: “A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.”

The operator apologized directly to the club, its new head coach and the players.

“I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.”

He also rejected any suggestion that Liverpool or another football club had been involved in his decision to film at Carrington.

“The video has been removed from my channel,” he added.

#2139. Jamie Carragher questions Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United appointment

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Carragher believes Mauricio Pochettino has as much to prove as Manchester United, suggesting the Argentine’s reputation is not fully backed up by his achievements.

Mauricio Pochettino is preparing for his first match in charge of Manchester United against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, following his departure from the United States national team to replace Michael Carrick.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager has arrived at Old Trafford with plenty of experience, but Carragher believes his appointment represents an opportunity for both United and Pochettino to rebuild their reputations.

Writing in The Telegraph, the former Liverpool defender highlighted the irony of United turning to a manager whose own career needs a fresh start.

“It is ironic that in their latest attempt to rejuvenate and restore some of their old fire, Manchester United have turned to a manager whose career needs a similar reawakening,” Carragher wrote.

He suggested that Pochettino should be grateful that a club of United’s stature came calling at this stage of his career.

“Manchester United need a savior to first ease them from the relegation zone and then revive their Premier League and Champions League credibility. Pochettino, meanwhile, needed a club like United to save him from a managerial career that promised more than it delivered.”

Manchester United were fortunate to secure a manager with Pochettino’s experience after dismissing Michael Carrick so early in the season. However, he believes the Argentine has plenty to prove despite his strong reputation in the game.

“The South American returns to England with a big reputation, but not enough on his CV to back up glowing testimonials,” he continued.

Carrick believes one of the biggest concerns surrounding Pochettino is his record in important matches.

“A recurring issue with Pochettino, which continued with the US team, is an inability to get over the line in the most consequential, winnable matches, resulting in a lack of big trophies.”

Despite questioning his ability to bottle in big games, he praised his teams when everything comes in together.

“Ten years ago his best team were the embodiment of him, full of energy, style and ambition. Time will tell whether this version of Pochettino is the one turning up at Old Trafford.”

Pochettino will have the chance to shut Carragher’s doubts on Sunday when Manchester United face Liverpool. His immediate priority will be to take United out of the relegation zone, but the expectations at Old Trafford will extend far beyond survival.

The Liverpool fixture will be his first opportunity to make an impression. Carragher, however, believes the Argentine’s real challenge is to turn his reputation into success.

#2137. He played for Nottingham Forest and West Ham - Then built a luxury cars business

Marlon Harewood enjoyed a glittering 18-year career in the professional game, and when he retired from playing he entered into a business in an area that's close to the hearts of many players.

Footballers, it's reasonable to say, have always been keen on their cars. The sight of Baby Bentleys and Land Rovers arriving at training grounds became a familiar one on transfer deadline days, an inevitable consequence of young men earning more money in a week than many of us do in a year.

So it makes perfect sense that going into the car industry makes perfect sense for a recently-retired professional footballer, and in the case of the former Nottingham Forest and West Ham United striker Marlon Harewood, an 18-year career in the professional game gave him the knowledge to be able to establish himself in a particular niche that was close to his very own heart.

Over a playing career that lasted from 1998 to 2016, Marlon Harewood played for fourteen different clubs in England, from the Premier League to the National League North, but it's for his spells with Nottingham Forest and West Ham United that he's best remembered.

Harewood came through the youth system at Nottingham Forest and went on to make just over 200 appearances for them between 1998 and 2004, with a brief spell back at The City Ground in 2011. His first spell began at the worst possible time. Having made his League debut as Forest sailed to promotion back to the Premier League, his first full season saw his team finishing bottom of the table on 30 points, eleven adrift of safety. He managed one goal in 23 League appearances.

What are your memories of Marlon Harewood as a player? Let us know in the comments below!

Things did improve for him. Harewood developed a strong partnership with David Johnson, and Forest reached the Championship play-offs off the back of his 20 league goals in the 2002-03 season. But they didn't go up, and in November 2003 he left for West Ham United.

He was more successful at West Ham than he had been at Nottingham Forest. He scored 13 in 28 in his first season in the Championship for them, and the following season scored 17 times as the Irons returned to the Premier League, while he also featured in the FA Cup final against Liverpool, where West Ham lost on penalties following a thrilling 3-3 draw. In his first season back in the Premier League since that disastrous first season with Nottingham Forest, he scored 14 times in 37 appearances.

Robert Huth became a key man for the Potters after his 2009 switch from Boro

Harewood's career started to slow when he moved from West Ham to Aston Villa in 2007, turning down a move to WIgan Athletic in order to do so. He found his opportunities at Villa Park to be severely limited, and in 2010 he was sent on loan to Wolverhampton Wanderers.

In sharp contrast to the first half of his career, which had only taken in two clubs, the second was far more nomadic. There was another permanent deal for him with Blackpool in 2010, but there were also spells on loan at Newcastle United and Barnsley, and even a spell with Guangzhou RF in the China Super League.

The last five years of his EFL career saw him play for four different clubs; a return to Forest, then Barnsley, Bristol City and Hartlepool United. And he called time on his playing career in 2016, after scoring ten goals in a season for Nuneaton Town of the National League North.

The automotive trade was an obvious next step for Harewood, who'd long had an appreciation for cars, and it was one that he'd been slowly working on behind the scenes for years. Initially founded while he was still playing for Forest, it was run by his business partner while his football career continued. When he retired from playing, he was able to move seamlessly into it.

But the business that he built up tailored to a very specific market of which he was a member; designing and customising cars for players through his company, AC13 Premier. By the end of 2022, his clients included Harry Kane and Kyle Walker. Speaking to The Daily Star in December of that year, he explained: "Everyone’s got an interest in cars at the highest level - people like their nice stuff and cars did it for me."

In moving from professional football to cars, Marlon Harewood has been fortunate to work in two industries that he enjoys, though this is also a reflection of his own range of talents.

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has been provided with a timely team news boost ahead of the Premier League showdown against Manchester United on Sunday.

With the international break now concluded, the Reds players who were away with their countries have now reconvened on Merseyside and were put through their paces at the AXA Training Centre on Thursday.

There were no fresh injury concerns arising from national team duties, and there had already been good news earlier in the week when Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni resumed first-team training as they both close in on long-awaited returns from lengthy absences.

As per Liverpool Echo, a number of Reds players who had been carrying slight knocks or been absent through injury prior to the international window are now on course to be available for the Man United fixture.

The Dutch trio of Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong all trained, with the captain skipping Netherlands duty due to a minor issue, the midfielder missing our last three games with a heel problem, and the right-back overcoming a muscle injury he sustained in mid-October.

Dominik Szoboszlai had played through a slight knee problem for Hungary in recent days, but he was involved in the session in Kirkby today, albeit with strapping on the affected area.

Two other notable inclusions were Alexis Mac Allister and Ronald Araujo, both of whom partook in training despite being just back from representing their countries in South America, although Bradley and Leoni weren’t involved in today’s session as their recoveries are being managed carefully.

#2135. Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang

Mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

“Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

There will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

As it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

There was also another promising performance by new signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

“They know how to do it,” Arteta said of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”

Coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

“Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they showed it,” Lampard said. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”

"They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard said Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt

Before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he said, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

If that was a case of Arteta talking the talk, then his players happily followed it up by walking the walk here. Arsenal played with an unmistakable swagger, as if they simply knew there would only be one outcome against a group of Coventry players with limited experience at this level.

The energy of the home supporters, as buoyant as you might expect following last season’s triumph, undoubtedly helped Arsenal. There were none of the nerves that defined the run-in in the spring, with the fans instead in a partying mood from the moment new signing Ezri Konsa was introduced to the Emirates Stadium before kick-off.

The opening goal took only 15 minutes to arrive, as Havertz swept in an accurate finish from Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross. It has been a good summer for Havertz, who missed so much of last season with injury but has found some rhythm over the past few months. Including friendlies and his performances for Germany at the World Cup, this was his 10th goal in his last 17 appearances.

Coventry have invested in some powerful, commanding players this summer, but there were signs that the physical battle was proving difficult for Lampard’s side. Caleb Yirenkyi is their new club-record signing in midfield, but he was brutally thrown to the floor by Lewis-Skelly in the first half.

Saka’s goal was the result of a quick cross by Tzolis, the new £34m winger who has made such an exciting start to his Arsenal career. The Greek forward was the star of the first half, constantly making things happen, and his delivery was diverted into Saka’s path after 23 minutes.

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Odegaard showed in the Community Shield that he is in a more confident place than the last campaign, when he constantly battled injuries, and his early-season form continued here. His goal was scruffy, bobbled in off the right foot, but his all-round performance was typically smooth. With two goals in two games, he has already beaten his tally from last season.

"It's a top finish I would say" 😂Martin Odegaard reacts to his goal against Coventry! pic.twitter.com/mciFfZ6Fhx

From there, the game was over. Arsenal could remove Saka, Rice and Odegaard, safe in the knowledge that their work was done. A comfortable night for the champions, and the perfect start.

"How are you going to keep everyone happy? Winning." 🔥Mikel Arteta reveals his secret for keeping his full squad content after Arsenal's 3-0 win against Coventry 👀 pic.twitter.com/IarLijhd6I

"I think we can do even better to be fair" Martin Odegaard reflects on Arsenal's win over Coventry in the first game of the season 💭 pic.twitter.com/nB2YW83VlE

It’s all over in the capital and Arsenal have started their reign as Premier League champions with a confident and assured three-goal victory over newly-promoted Coventry. Havertz, Saka and Odegaard were all on target in a flawless team performance from Arteta’s men. It’s been a tough evening for Lampard’s side, who simply couldn’t handle Arsenal.

FULL-TIME: Arsenal cruise to victory against Coventry on the opening day of the new season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/ctybTEor9J

There will be four minutes of added time to round this game off. Merino shoots from long range and aims for the bottom corner, but Rushworth dives to his left and makes the stop.

Awoniyi tries to make a run in behind Arsenal’s defence and latch onto Hamer’s pass. The striker is hauled to the ground by Mosquera, who is lucky to escape a booking. The resulting delivery is smacked straight out of play by Torp. That is such a disappointing cross.

Torp swings a cross into Rudoni, who makes a run from deep. Rudoni meets the delivery, but his glancing header is straight at Raya. It’s Coventry’s best chance of the match but they’ve failed to convert it. Arsenal’s clean sheet remains intact.

Arteta makes his fifth and final substitution as Calafiori, who recorded the assist for Arsenal’s opener, is withdrawn for Hincapie.

Lampard responds with his own alteration, bringing Hamer on for Tchaouna.

Coventry are still waiting for their first shot on target this evening. Arsenal are seeing this game out with exemplary professionalism.

Odegaard and Tzolis are the next players to leave the field. Eze and World Cup winner Merino are on as their replacements. Arteta’s substitutions tonight have underlined Arsenal’s tremendous squad depth, and that is without the involvement of both Guimaraes and Konsa.

Lewis-Skelly tries to slide a pinpoint pass through to Calafiori, in an attempt to recreate Arsenal’s opening goal from their Community Shield triumph. It nutmegs Torp, but Rushworth makes a quick dash off his line to collect the ball and eliminate any danger.

Lampard adds some fresh legs and orders a double change. Awoniyi, who makes his Coventry debut, and Rudoni are on, with Simms and Thomas-Asante taken off.

Here come some Arsenal changes. Rice and Saka depart to loud ovations, with Zubimendi and Madueke on to replace them.

Tzolis motors into the Coventry penalty area once again and picks out Havertz, who makes a intelligent run across the six-yard box. Before he can cross or shoot, Thomas sprints over to make an interception.

The visitors then fail to clear a corner and Tzolis slams a low, powerful effort at goal. Rushworth gets down low and spills it, but Thomas is there to hack it away.

Lampard makes the first change of the match for either side as Torp replaces Yirenkyi, whose endured a difficult debut in central midfield for his new side.

Odegaard is enjoying himself out there this evening. Just as he did against Manchester City, he’s playing with such authority, purpose and confidence.

The ball breaks to Tzolis who unleashes a venomous effort at goal. It takes a big deflection and flies out for a corner.

From a Coventry corner, Arsenal counter attack with such intensity and speed. The move ends as Odegaard attempts to find Tzolis with a through ball, but the Norwegian overhits the pass and delayed it too long. The offside flag is then raised against Tzolis.

Van Ewijk attempts to find Simms with a chipped cross towards the back post, but it’s marginally over the striker’s head as Coventry step up their search to pull a goal back.

It’s a nightmare start to the second half for Coventry. Whatever Arteta said to his players at the break has worked wonders.

Lewis-Skelly then shoots from long range and his shot is tipped over the bar by Rushworth.

White overlaps Saka and latches onto the winger’s pass. Saka then tees up Odegaard, who scuffs his close-range effort. Rushworth is wrong-footed and despite getting a glove to it, the ball trickles into the net and Arsenal are cruising.

It's Martin Odegaard... Arsenal have three! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/LrqSSGJWE6

Odegaard has scored some beautiful goals in an Arsenal shirt. That wasn’t one of them. He won’t care, though. Two goals in two games for the Arsenal captain.

Read more about his return to form here: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/08/21/odegaard-a-man-possessed-in-bid-to-unlock-arsenal-attack/

We are back under way for the second half. Will Arsenal add more goals to their tally or can Coventry produce a memorable comeback?

It’s been a steep learning curve for the newly-promoted side, who have been overpowered and outclassed by Arsenal’s quality.

Arsenal are in complete control thanks to a commanding first half display against Coventry. Havertz and Saka have the goals, with the reigning Premier League champions on course to claim a routine three points to kickstart their title defence.

Once again, Saka plays a short corner. Odegaard then passes to Rice, who is in acres of space on the edge of the penalty area. The midfielder shoots, but his curling effort drifts narrowly wide of the far post.

There will be two minutes of added time at the end of this half.

The ball bobbles into Tchaouna’s path and the winger tries a very ambitious acrobatic effort from the edge of the box. It had Raya worried for a second, but the effort lands on the roof of the net. That would have been a spectacular goal if it had sneaked in.

Tzolis teases Thomas and works some space before clipping a cross in towards Havertz. The forward doesn’t connect with the header and Coventry scramble it clear.

Odegaard is pulling the strings and slips a delightful pass through to the onrushing White, who finds himself very far forward, but the right back is swiftly closed down by Coventry’s defence as he shoots.

At the other end, Simms does brilliantly to turn Gabriel and win a free kick just outside the box. The Brazilian centre back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

Coventry are feeling the full effects of the stark difference in levels between Championship and Premier League. Arsenal look streets ahead at the moment.

Christos Tzolis has only played a few games for Arsenal but it’s already easy to see why he registered 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He has shown on numerous occasions this summer that he is willing to cross the ball as soon as he receives it. No delay, no faff. It worked against Manchester City last weekend and it created Saka’s goal here.

Welcome back to the Premier League, Coventry... It’s been a chastening opening 27 minutes for Lampard’s side.

Yirenkyi then receives a yellow card on his debut for pulling Lewis-Skelly’s shirt.

Rice strides through midfield and plays a one-two with Odegaard. The English midfielder tees up Tzolis, whose fires a cross into the corridor of uncertainty. Rushworth parries it into the danger zone, gifting an unmarked Saka a simple finish from close range. What a start for the champions!

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Arsenal are purring and oozing confidence. Coventry need to be careful and must stay in this game. They cannot allow Arsenal to get a second and run away with this.

Coventry had started well but their first error in defence was ruthlessly punished. That’s Havertz’s 10th goal in his last 17 matches for club and country (including pre-season friendlies). After such an injury-disrupted campaign last year, he’s had a very good summer.

Van Ewijk fails to clear his lines and he’s closed down by Tzolis. The ball ricochets into Calafiori’s path and the left back picks out Havertz with a low cross.

The German sweeps a composed shot into the bottom corner. It’s such a cultured finish and Arsenal begin their defence of the Premier League with a 1-0 lead after 15 minutes.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

Some steady possession for Coventry, who are looking to take the sting and excitement out of the game while also calming the buoyant Arsenal fans down.

Tzolis pops up on the right wing and latches onto Rice’s pass. The attacker then delivers a first-time cross into the box which finds Saka, whose half-volley is blocked by Amenda.

Arsenal then work a short corner that ends with White teeing up Tzolis, but his low strike is smothered by Coventry’s defence. Tzolis has certainly made a lively start, and unsurprisingly, Arsenal’s set pieces are causing some early problems.

Tzolis looks dangerous as he dribbles at Van Ewijk, before cutting inside and unleashing a powerful shot. However, his effort is high and wide. Nevertheless, it’s positive play from Arsenal’s new signing.

Following that Coventry corner, the Premier League holders have monopolised the possession in the early minutes. Chants of ‘Champions of England, we know what we are’ ring around the stadium thanks to the home support, who are in full voice.

Coventry get us under way and the newly-promoted side have won an early corner, which is comfortably dealt with by Arsenal’s defence.

The atmosphere at the Emirates is electric. Can Arsenal flex their title-winning credentials once again or will Coventry cause an almighty upset?

New Arsenal signing Ezri Konsa has been presented on the pitch, with both sets of players set to follow him any moment now.

The 2026-27 season is just minutes away from kicking off.

Coventry have recruited some powerful, aggressive players this summer. They will be looking to frustrate Arsenal by shutting down the spaces around their penalty area, and they will certainly be competitive at set-pieces.

Meanwhile, the Arsenal fans have just had their first glimpse of Ezri Konsa in the club’s shirt. The new signing walked out onto the pitch to wave to the supporters.

With just over five minutes until the 2026-27 Premier League season starts, here are tonight’s teams in full...

Arsenal: Raya, White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori, Odegaard, Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.

Subs: Arrizabalaga, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Nwaneri, Merino, Zubimendi, Dowman.

Coventry: Rushworth, van Ewijk, Thomas, Amenda, Dasilva, Onyeka, Yirenkyi, Grimes, Thomas-Asante, Simms, Tchaouna.

Subs: Wilson, Rudoni, Sakamoto, Awoniyi, Kitching, Latibeaudiere, Eccles, Overgaard, Hamer.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “He had a slight tension in his groin. He hasn’t done a pre-season, he only had four or five days before that [Man City] game. We have to take a lot of new stuff for him as well. We need to take it bit by bit.”

Another game, another snub for Gabriel Martinelli. As was the case against Manchester City in last weekend’s Community Shield, the Brazilian isn’t even on the bench tonight. It’s quite clear what’s going on here: Arsenal need to make sales and he is an obvious candidate to depart. It’s not particularly pleasant, though, and you can’t help but feel for a player who has been so important to this club over the last seven years.

Martinelli has made it clear he does not want to move to Galatasary, who made an offer recently. Will a more suitable club come forward for him? We’ll find out in the coming days.

In two full seasons at Coventry between 2021 and 2023, Viktor Gyokeres scored 40 goals in 97 games for Coventry, and was part of the side that lost on penalties to Luton Town in the Championship play-off final to Luton Town.

If Coventry had won that game, would Gyokeres still be wearing a sky blue shirt instead of joining Sporting CP and then Arsenal, who knows...

The striker will have to wait to get onto the pitch against his former team, with Mikel Arteta choosing Kai Havertz to lead the line.

Odegaard comes into the new Premier League season, which begins when Arsenal host Coventry City on Friday night, with a point to prove. That may sound unusual, given his new-found status as a title-winning captain, but last year was a strange one for the 27-year-old. The club’s most successful campaign of his time at Arsenal was also the most frustrating one for Odegaard as an individual.

Last season, Arsenal clinched a much-anticipated Premier League title for the first time in 22 years and are the favourites to lift the trophy for a second successive season. Mikel Arteta’s side have recently claimed the Community Shield and look like they mean business.

Arsenal are clearly not resting on their laurels in their bid to win another top-flight title, having strengthened their squad this summer with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa.

Arteta looks raring to go and ready to mount another title charge.

"Everything has to start with me" 💪Mikel Arteta says Arsenal are ready for the new Premier League season 💥 pic.twitter.com/rsUcs7ot7T

After last season’s Championship by a whopping 95 points under Frank Lampard’s management, Coventry head into their first Premier League campaign since suffering relegation from the competition in 2001.

Coventry were playing in the fourth tier as recently as 2017, so lining up against the Premier League holders is a full-circle moment for the club and supporters that is richly deserved.

"I loved it, I loved driving here, feeling the atmosphere, the fans" Frank Lampard on what tonight means for him and Coventry 😍Watch live here: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/077Bga2Z4W

On Friday night, at the home of champions Arsenal, Coventry officially begin a new chapter back in the Premier League and expectations will be high. The man responsible for that tidal wave of optimism is Lampard, their promotion hero.

He has proved a transformative appointment since arriving in November 2024, and the former England and Chelsea captain is relishing the chance to rattle some cages.

His return is a feel-good story and Lampard has a point to prove. He admits that the desire to upset his detractors drives him on. “I’ve got experience of the Premier League and hopefully I can get that across to the players,” he said.

“The club has been out of this division for 25 years so of course it’s exciting. We want to challenge and we want to do well. I’m pleased that we’re here and you want to work at the top. We’re very focused on the job.”

Arsenal ruined Enzo Maresca’s first competitive outing as Man City’s new manager in the club’s first match without Pep Guardiola. It was one-way traffic as Arsenal cruised to a resounding 3-0 win to lift the Community Shield in Cardiff.

Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring just 23 seconds after he was brilliantly played in by Myles Lewis-Skelly’s defence-splitting pass. Arsenal doubled their lead before the half-hour mark through Kai Havertz’s close-range header and Martin Odegaard added a sumptuously taken third shortly after the interval.

The Premier League holders were in a ruthless mood and completely overran their opponents. Christos Tzolis grabbed two assists out on the left wing, Bruno Guimarães produced a typically commanding performance in the first half and Odegaard controlled proceedings with his creativity.

It was an early taste of silverware for Mikel Arteta’s men, who are the overwhelming favourites to retain their Premier League crown.

"I'm really pleased, that's a really good team" Ian Wright is happy with the Arsenal starting XI to face Coventry, do you agree? 💬 Watch live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/IUBlMS963w

New signings Aurele Amenda, Loum Tchaouna and Caleb Yirenkyi all start and make their Coventry debuts this evening.

Carl Rushworth and Frank Onyeka also begin from the outset after making their moves permanent following successful loans last season.

Your City tonight. 📋 pic.twitter.com/V0nzaemLYF

As Sam Dean confirmed earlier on, Bruno Guimaraes is absent from the squad. The Brazilian was subbed off at half-time in the dominant Community Shield victory over Manchester City with a thigh issue.

Both Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka start after being used off the bench in the Community Shield last weekend, with Guimaraes and Noni Madueke dropping to the bench.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your Premier League opening day XI ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/yRf2BEs3BA

To soften the blow of Bruno Guimaraes’ absence from tonight’s squad due to injury, the Premier League holders can rejoice over the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for over £50m.

The centre back has penned a four-year deal with the option of a further year.

Speaking to Arsenal’s official website, Sporting Director Andrea Berta said: “Ezri is a defender of high quality, whose athleticism, composure and tactical intelligence have established him as one of the Premier League’s most consistent performers.

“Being comfortable in both central defence and at right-back, Ezri will bring valuable versatility to our squad while maintaining the high defensive standards which are fundamental to our challenge of winning major trophies.”

Konsa will play no role in tonight’s encounter, having only completed the move earlier in the day.

Reinforcing the backline ✍️ pic.twitter.com/deYQhZcmOy

Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

#2134. Mauricio Pochettino outlines transfer plans and addresses Bruno Fernandes controversy

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Mauricio Pochettino has made it clear he wants to be involved in Manchester United’s major squad decisions, while also addressing questions surrounding captain Bruno Fernandes ahead of his first game against Liverpool.

The new Manchester United head coach explained that he wants to have a voice in decisions that shape the squad.

“Sometimes maybe you are a coach and maybe you have more power in the decisions,” Pochettino said in his first Manchester United press conference.

“It depends on the structure, it depends on the communication, the relationships, you know, with all the areas.”

Mauricio Pochettino highlighted his responsibilities are clear about who he selects and plays in games.]

“I am the guy that is going to decide the squad for Sunday, and I’m going to pick the team, I’m going to make the changes, and of course in the future, I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen on the squad.”

Pochettino was also asked about Bruno Fernandes, whose critical comments about Michael Carrick’s tactics became a talking point during the former manager’s final weeks at Old Trafford.

The Argentine was really keen about the squad’s commitment, dodging the blame on Fernandes and describing Fernandes as a key figure in the dressing room.

“The commitment from all the players was amazing from day one,” he said.

“Bruno is our captain and a very important player but all the players need to feel they are important from the bottom to the top.”

Pochettino revealed that he had already spent time speaking with the players to understand their situation both on and off the pitch.

“Yesterday we spent three hours chatting to the players in my office and maybe I missed the injured players.”

Pochettino admitted the first few days at United had been extremely busy as he tried to get up to speed before his first match.

He is excited by the opportunity but knows there is little time to prepare for Sunday’s trip to Anfield.

“It’s a happy time but at the same time, so busy,” he explained.

“It’s been about adapting in the last few days, and it’s a race to arrive in condition to be competitive against Liverpool, and now our focus is 100 per cent on Liverpool in the game on Sunday.”

#2133. Moises Caicedo And Kendry Paez Give Chelsea World Cup Signal

Ecuador’s late World Cup surge has given Chelsea a useful development signal through Moises Caicedo and Kendry Paez before Xabi Alonso’s first pre-season friendly on 28 July.

Chelsea confirmed that Caicedo and Paez reached the Round of 32 after Ecuador’s dramatic 2-1 win over Germany.

For Alonso, the contrast between the two Chelsea midfielders matters as much as the result.

Caicedo captained Ecuador through the pressure game, with We Ain’t Got No History highlighting the Chelsea midfielder’s leadership role in a win that rescued their tournament.

Paez, meanwhile, sits in a different phase of his rise.

That should not worry Chelsea. FIFA identified Paez as one of the tournament’s wonderkids, but Chelsea’s bigger win is that he can absorb elite-tournament preparation without carrying a defining role too soon.

Read Chelsea has already looked at how Alonso must handle Paez’s development curve, and this knockout place sharpens that argument.

Alonso inherits a midfield loaded with senior names, transfer noise and immediate pressure.

Caicedo gives Chelsea the proven pillar. Paez gives them the controlled upside.

Ecuador’s run now gives Chelsea both at once.

For Chelsea, that is the ideal succession picture: leadership today, patience for tomorrow.

#2132. Omar Berrada breaks silence on Bruno Fernandes contract as Pochettino makes feelings clear

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Bruno Fernandes has been at the center of contract talks this season and is yet to sign a new deal at Manchester United.

Various reports have indicated that Bruno Fernandes has turned down two contract offers. He reportedly wants a 4-year deal but United are wary of such a deal as he is already 32 years old.

Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has confirmed the club are discussing a new contract with Bruno Fernandes, but has refused to reveal any details about the negotiations as the midfielder approaches the final months of his current deal.

Fernandes’ contract expires at the end of the season, leaving Manchester United with an important decision to make over the future of their captain.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Berrada praised the Portuguese international for his contribution to the club and made clear how highly he is valued at Old Trafford.

“Listen, I’ve said before, we have a tremendous amount of respect for Bruno,” Berrada said.

“We’re very fortunate to have him as a captain.

“What he’s done for this team over the last six, seven years is absolutely incredible. Last year he won, I think, all the individual awards that you can win.

“And we’re very proud to have him as captain. It’s true that we’re having conversations about his new contract, but I prefer to keep that private.

“I think it’s something that needs to be discussed behind the scenes between him and the club.”

Although contract talks are taking place, there is no indication of how close the two parties are to reaching an agreement. United will be keen to avoid losing one of their most influential players throughout these years, but the terms and length of any new contract remain speculative at the moment.

New manager, Mauricio Pochettino, has backed his captain ahead of his first game against Liverpool. He was asked about Bruno Fernandes, whose critical comments about Michael Carrick’s tactics became a talking point during the former manager’s final weeks at Old Trafford.

The new head coach did not get drawn into the controversy, instead stressing the importance of Fernandes to the team and the need for every player to feel valued.

“Bruno is our captain and a very important player but all the players need to feel they are important from the bottom to the top,” Pochettino said.

The Bruno Fernandes contract situation comes at a difficult time for United, who are 18th in the Premier League with eight points from their opening 10 matches. They have managed just one win and five draws during that run.

Pochettino has inherited a struggling side, and keeping Bruno Fernandes committed to the project could prove important as he is one of the few performing stars in the fragile Manchester United team.

#2131. Chelsea World Cup Knockout Load Gives Xabi Alonso Pre-Season Problem

Chelsea’s World Cup contingent has moved from a group-stage watchlist into a genuine Xabi Alonso planning problem.

Chelsea’s own tournament update confirms that Enzo Fernandez, Mike Penders, Moises Caicedo, Kendry Paez, Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato have reached the Round of 32.

England have also progressed after their final Group L win over Panama, which keeps Reece James and Trevoh Chalobah inside the wider knockout picture.

For supporters, that is a status marker. For Alonso, it is where summer pride starts to become pre-season compression.

The concern is not simply volume. It is where the minutes are landing.

Enzo has not missed a minute for Argentina, while Caicedo has remained central for Ecuador and captained them in the 2-1 win over Germany.

Those are not fringe workloads. They are the two midfield profiles Chelsea have built large parts of their control game around.

Alonso’s first Chelsea pre-season was always going to demand clarity through the middle of the pitch.

Instead, the players most central to that reset are still operating in knockout football.

Caicedo’s Ecuador role is the cleanest example. Read Chelsea has already assessed how his captaincy display against Germany strengthened his leadership case, but the next layer is more complicated.

Every additional knockout tie gives him more tournament rhythm, more authority and more fatigue.

Argentina’s route against Cape Verde keeps him on a glamorous stage at exactly the moment Chelsea need to settle his role, mood and tactical responsibilities under Alonso.

If Madrid-related noise continues around him, the club cannot afford a sluggish July handover.

Reece James started England’s first two matches before a hamstring issue ruled him out of the Panama game, according to the Guardian.

England still topped the group and moved into a last-32 tie with DR Congo, but James’ situation is exactly the kind of detail Chelsea’s medical team will monitor closely.

Chelsea have already had to plan around a large World Cup group.

The broader issue was clear in Read Chelsea’s earlier pre-season workload piece, but the knockout stage sharpens it because the returns will now be staggered.

Enzo brings a maximum group-stage load. Caicedo brings captaincy responsibility and heavy Ecuador minutes.

James brings knockout qualification mixed with another hamstring-management question.

Gusto and Hato remain tied to France and the Netherlands, while Penders and Paez are still absorbing tournament environments before club reintegration.

That is a spine issue, not a fringe issue.

Alonso needs automatisms in possession, spacing around the double pivot, clearer full-back behaviour and pressing triggers from midfield.

Those details do not bed in properly when key players arrive in drips after a major summer tournament.

Players returning from knockout football can bring competitive sharpness that closed-door friendlies cannot replicate.

Caicedo captaining Ecuador through pressure games matters. Enzo playing high-leverage minutes for Argentina matters.

Gusto and Hato absorbing tournament detail also helps Chelsea’s defensive reset.

But Chelsea cannot treat every tournament minute as clean preparation.

Alonso must decide who returns straight into tactical work, who needs a genuine pause and who can handle August without creating an avoidable injury bill by September.

That is where the James situation feels central.

If Chelsea’s captain carries a World Cup hamstring warning, the club’s right-sided structure becomes more than a selection debate.

It becomes an availability question that touches Gusto, the wider defensive rebuild and the need for control from midfield.

Read Chelsea has already looked at James’ captaincy test under Alonso, and the injury layer now makes that test sharper.

This is the hidden cost of a strong international footprint.

Chelsea want players good enough to survive deep into tournaments.

Alonso now has to make sure that status does not leave his first league weeks short of the very control those players are meant to provide.
